it’s a stack that feels instant, trustworthy, and impossible to leave.

Right now the highest-value path is clear:

Make outgoing VoIP connect every time.
Separate outgoing UI from incoming UI so call state always looks correct.
Make notifications first-class: full name, avatar, fast open, lock-screen reply, reliable actions.
Make media bulletproof: audio route, mic, speaker, Bluetooth, reconnect, call recovery.
Add identity and trust: caller verification, spam scoring, Truecaller-grade lookup, business identity.
Add AI that is actually useful: live translation, summaries, smart voicemail, call screening, follow-up drafting.
Make it feel faster than native dialers: prewarm WebRTC, instant call screen, zero ghost states, no ANRs.
For this codebase, the next engineering milestone is:

Fix VoIP phone-account registration/routing so outgoing calls bind to ChatrConnectionService and hit NativeWebRtcEngine.startAsCaller(...).
Replace the reused incoming screen with a real outgoing call screen/state model.
Finish live device verification for connect, mute, speaker, hold, end, reconnect, and lock-screen notification actions.
